school: Structural Biology, Cryo-Electron Microscopy, Biophysics, Molecular Biology
legacy: Yifan Cheng helped revolutionize the ability of scientists to observe biological molecules at near-atomic resolution. Through advancements in cryo-electron microscopy and structural biology, he contributed to techniques that allow researchers to visualize complex molecular machines in unprecedented detail. His work accelerated discoveries across biology, medicine, and biotechnology by making previously inaccessible molecular structures observable.
earlyLife: Cheng developed a strong interest in science, mathematics, and the natural world during his education in China. Fascinated by how biological systems function at microscopic scales, he pursued studies that combined physics and biology. This interdisciplinary background led him toward structural biology, where he sought to understand life by examining the architecture of its molecular components.
scientificField: Structural Biology, Biophysics, Molecular Biology, Cryo-Electron Microscopy
majorContributions: Cheng contributed extensively to the development and application of cryo-electron microscopy techniques that enable researchers to reconstruct detailed three-dimensional structures of biological molecules. His research advanced understanding of membrane proteins, ribosomes, ion channels, and other essential cellular machinery. By improving image acquisition, computational reconstruction, and structural analysis methods, he helped transform cryo-electron microscopy into one of the most powerful tools in modern biological science.
laterLife: During the later stages of his career, Cheng continued leading research efforts focused on revealing the molecular mechanisms underlying biological function and disease. He remained active in mentoring scientists, advancing imaging technologies, and expanding the capabilities of structural biology. His work continued to influence biomedical research and the development of new therapeutic strategies.
whyImportant: Many advances in modern medicine depend upon understanding the structures of the molecules that drive life. Cheng's contributions helped make these structures visible with exceptional precision, accelerating research into diseases, drug development, and fundamental biological processes. His work strengthened one of the most transformative technologies in contemporary life science.
